item.title: Flu impacting local hospital
item.description: Flu continues to impact wards at Sligo University Hospital. There are currently four outbreaks in separate wards. A plea has been re-issued to those with flu-like symptoms not to visit the facility. Advertisement The four outbreaks are less than the six which were reported on December 17th. 19 patients with flu are being treated across the hospital. item.title: Busiest year on record at Ireland West Airport
item.description: Ireland West Airport recorded its busiest year ever in 2025, with passenger numbers reaching over 946 thousand passengers. This is a 13.5 per cent increase on 2024. The airport now serves 21 international destinations with over 96 thousand passengers travelling on the London Heathrow service alone. Advertisement August was the busiest month in the airport's history, with over 106 thousand passengers.

item.title: Currently no plans to introduce paid parking in Roscommon
item.description: There are currently no plans to introduce paid parking in Roscommon Town. That's according to Roscommon County Council Chief Executive Shane Tiernan. Paid parking is in operation in local towns such as Carrick on Shannon and Longford however it has not been introduced in Roscommon. Tiernan says no discussions have taken place so far: Advertisement

item.title: Further calls for minor injury unit to be developed in Longford town
item.description: There are calls for a minor injury unit and dialysis service to be developed in Longford town. Two local Fine Gael politicians say the existing St Joseph's site in the town could be used for the project. Deputy Micheál Carrigy and Cllr Peggy Nolan want an expanded consultant-led medical campus. item.title: Plans to reduce speed limits on national roads, says Minister
item.description: The Junior Transport Minister says there are plans to reduce speed limits on National Primary and Secondary roads. This would affect roads like the N4 Carrick-on-Shannon to Longford route and the N61 connecting Roscommon to Athlone. Speed limits on local roads were reduced to 60km per hour last year whilst there are also now plans to reduce speed limits on roads in urban areas. item.title: Roscommon Cllr against plans to reduce speed limits on National routes
item.description: A Roscommon councillor says he wouldn't be in favour of plans to reduce speed limits on National Primary and Secondary roads. Junior Transport Minister Sean Canney confirmed today they are looking at reducing the speed limit from 100 to 80km per hour. This would affect roads like the N4 Carrick on Shannon to Longford route and the N61 connecting Roscommon to Athlone. item.title: Climate action course to take place in Longford this month
item.description: Longford County Council will host a free climate action course for the over 55s this month. It'll be hosted by former UN diplomat Jacinta Barrins and the local authority's climate change officer. The course will highlight everyday actions that can help lower greenhouse gas emissions. The first of six classes will take place next Tuesday at Edgeworthstown Library. Climate Mentor Jacinta Barrins has been presenting the course across the country.
